extracted.intended_audience: law students, patent practitioners, and judges studying reissue/renewal and assignment rules
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory legal rules governing (1) surrender/reissue and renewal of patents (including disclaimers and term/extension effects) and (2) assignment and recording of patent interests (including effects in bankruptcy and on suits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's grant conclusive as to facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of an amended patent by the Commissioner of Patents is conclusive as to the existence of all the facts which were by law necessary to entitle him to issue it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conclusiveness applies in the absence of any controlling provisions, and except where it is apparent on the face of the patent (without auxiliary evidence) that the Commissioner was guilty of a clear excess of authority or that the patent was procured by fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for defective or insufficient specification (Act of 1836 §13)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective or insufficient description or specification, or by reason of claiming more than the inventor had a right to claim as new, if the error arose by inadvertence, mistake, or accident and without fraudulent intention, the Commissioner may, upon surrender and payment, issue a new patent for the residue of the unexpired term in accordance with the corrected description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory procedure: surrender the patent, pay the fee (historically $15), and the Commissioner may issue new letters for the same invention for the unexpired period. The statute also contemplates adding subsequently-invented improvements by similar proceedings (and may require disclaimers or specification alterations per the Commissioner's decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee may omit parts in a renewed patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reissue/renewal a patentee is not required to claim all things that were claimed in the original patent; he may omit portions of his original invention in a renewed patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omissions may be proper to avoid overclaiming or misleading the public, may be done by the patentee's choice, or may be required by the Commissioner. Omitting part of an invention harms no public policy because the public may then use what is given up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewed patent term and relation back
rubrics_metrics.description: A renewed (reissued) patent is granted for the unexpired term, commencing from the date of the original patent surrendered, and operates from the commencement of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently a renewed patent enures to the benefit of assignees who became such before renewal. New letters issued on surrender should generally relate back to the original grant's commencement and operate from that time for most purposes (subject to noted exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender and renewal may be made during extended term
rubrics_metrics.description: A surrender of letters-patent for a defective specification and issuance of a new patent (renewal/reissue) may lawfully be made at any time during an extended term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical case examples (e.g., Woodworth) show surrender and issuance of new letters during extension/extended terms; the new patent is treated as operating from the original commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer for inadvertent overbroad claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications may be amended by filing a disclaimer when, through inadvertence, accident, or mistake, the original claim was too broad (claiming more than the patentee was the original inventor of), provided some material and substantial part of the thing patented is truly the patentee's own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimer may be filed in the Patent Office by the patentee, administrator, executors, or assigns, of the whole or of a sectional interest; the disclaimer will be thereafter taken and considered part of the original specification to the extent of the disclaimant's interest and by those claiming under him subsequent to record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent extension procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be extended by special Acts of Congress, and by statutory procedure the Secretary of State, the Commissioner of Patents, and the Solicitor of the Treasury were constituted a board to hear evidence and decide whether extension is just and proper, considering public interest and reasonable remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later statutes vested the power solely in the Commissioner of Patents who must refer an application to the principal examiner for the class and grant or refuse on the same principles. Subsequent statute (May 27, 1848) declared no patent shall be extended for longer than seven years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation requirement for assignments (three classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent is assignable in law; assignments and every grant or conveyance of the exclusive right under a patent (to make and use, and to grant others to make and use within any specified part of the United States) shall be recorded in the Patent Office within three months from execution, for which a fee is payable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three classes required to be recorded: assignment of the whole patent; assignment of an undivided part; and grant/conveyance of exclusive right for any specified territorial part of the United States. Historically the fee was three dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording requirement is directory (protects purchasers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory requirement to record an assignment within three months is construed as directory rather than a prerequisite to the assignment's validity as between parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: recording protects bona fide purchasers without notice; failure to record within three months may prejudice the assignee in favor of a subsequent bona fide purchaser, but does not render the assignment void between the original parties. Recording at any time before trial/hearing is sufficient for purposes of a suit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-recording against wrongdoers and purchasers
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-recording of an assignment should not give advantage to mere wrongdoers, and should not allow infringers to rely on an assignee's failure to record as a defense; but a bona fide purchaser without notice within the statutory period may be preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where recording was omitted, equity favors treating the provision as directory; wrongdoers acted 'in fraudem legis' and should not benefit. A prior bona fide purchaser (in time) may be preferred on the ground of laches if the assignment was not recorded within the statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment vests indefeasible interest; surrender cannot defeat assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment vests in the assignee an interest in the patent indefeasible by act of the patentee, so that the patentee cannot (by surrender of his patent) affect the rights of an assignee previously granted any interest without the assignee's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory surrender and reissue provisions expressly save the rights of assignees; strictly an assignee should be a party to a surrender, but where he is not, prior assignments are not vacated and the patent remains the same in contemplation of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments before patent issue and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention may be assigned for the patent before it is taken out so as to vest in the assignee the exclusive interest when the patent issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: the application must be made and the specification duly sworn to by the inventor, and the assignment must be recorded. Specific performance in equity may be ordered to enforce such contractual conveyances of future inventions or improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and bankruptcy — limits and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent already obtained passes to assignees in bankruptcy; under some systems an invention perfected and for which application has been made will pass to assignees, but mere schemes in the head or unpatented-perfected inventions where no application was made present more difficult questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law tends to treat the interest as acquired upon application for a patent; materials incorporating the invention would pass as property, but whether the invention itself (absent application) passes is doubtful and fact-dependent.

rubrics_metrics.name: New letters on surrender generally relate back
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is surrendered and new letters are issued upon an amended specification, the new letters are generally regarded as relating back to the commencement of the original term and should operate from that time for many purposes (though not necessarily all).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If treated otherwise, new letters would be a new patent running from their date; but where the new letters recite the facts of surrender and amendment, courts have held they cover only the same invention and the same term as the original (subject to exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable relief (injunction quia timet) on apprehension of infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill in equity for an injunction (quia timet) will lie where the patent right is admitted or established and there is well-grounded proof of an apprehended intention of the defendant to violate the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An injunction already granted (or existence of a pending injunction) is prima facie evidence of intended violation; suits in equity differ from actions at law in this respect and do not always require a completed prior breach to obtain relief.
